commit message:
Fix method overwrite warning when loading the package (#255)

This was caused by providing a default value of `nothing` for the
`model` argument in the `Problem` constructor, which ends up creating a
two-argument method that is also created further down by virtue of using
default values.

By simply removing the default value for `model`, we remain at feature
parity with the methods prior to the change and we don't overwrite
anything.

author: Alex Arslan <ararslan@comcast.net>
commit message:
Fix use of norm and remove vecnorm

The behavior of `norm(x, p)` for matrices changed in Julia PR 27401 to
be the same as `norm(vec(x), p)` and `vecnorm` was removed. The previous
behavior of `norm` for matrices is now captured by `opnorm`. This
updates our extensions to these functions to match, and emits
deprecation warnings as appropriate.

As a somewhat related change, this also deprecates the positional
dimension argument to `sum` in favor of keyword arguments, in keeping
with Base.

commit message:
Fix method overwrite warning when loading the package

This was caused by providing a default value of `nothing` for the
`model` argument in the `Problem` constructor, which ends up creating a
two-argument method that is also created further down by virtue of using
default values.

By simply removing the default value for `model`, we remain at feature
parity with the methods prior to the change and we don't overwrite
anything.

significant memory savings.

author: Alex Arslan <ararslan@comcast.net>
commit message:
Load solver packages using Requires.jl

Currently the package implements its own version of optional
dependencies which checks the current user's package installation
directories for the given solver packages. This has issues both with
precompilation and with Pkg in Julia 0.7 and higher.

Now, historically the Requires package has been a hack, but a recent
overhaul makes it more legit to use. It is currently the best, if only,
solution to optional dependencies.

This change moves all solver selection logic into Requires. This should
be largely user-invisible, with the very notable exception that the
first matching solver package is NOT automatically loaded; the user will
now need to explicitly load a solver package in order to use Convex.
The order of `using Convex` and `using SomeSolver` does not matter,
however.

`objectid` returns `UInt32` on 32-bit systems. Currently `ConicObj` only
accepts indexing operations with `UInt64` keys, which causes a method
error on 32-bit systems. This was an oversight when introducing
`ConicObj` as its own type.

Fixes #272

Parameterize Constant on the type of its value

This allows for more expressive condition checking using dispatch, as
complex numbers, real numbers, or arrays thereof can be handled as
separate methods.

This also limits the types that can be accepted as constant values to
scalars, vectors, and matrices. Previously this was assumed but not
actually checked.

commit message:
Fix use of norm and remove vecnorm

The behavior of `norm(x, p)` for matrices changed in Julia PR 27401 to
be the same as `norm(vec(x), p)` and `vecnorm` was removed. The previous
behavior of `norm` for matrices is now captured by `opnorm`. This
updates our extensions to these functions to match, and emits
deprecation warnings as appropriate.

As a somewhat related change, this also deprecates the positional
dimension argument to `sum` in favor of keyword arguments, in keeping
with Base.

commit message:
Use semver for compatibility bounds, drop Julia 0.7

Julia 0.7 is no longer maintained so we'd might as well set our lower
bound at 1.0, the current LTS release.

Using `^` (semver compat) instead of `>=` for version bounds is safer as
it ensures that, assuming package authors are actually obeying semver,
we aren't immediately opting into potentially breaking changes.

Optimizer.optimize(), similar to how it is done in the IRC classes.

If align is set to True in COS optimizations, then the Optimizer base
class will call fit_rigid/_fit_rigid in the main optimization loop.

Optimizer.fit_rigid(). If the method is not present, the optimizer will
fall back to self._fit_rigid(), that aligns coordinates, steps and
forces.

author: Marclie <mliebenthal@fsu.edu>
commit message:
Calculations whose energy depends on the orientation of the molecule has difficulties with alignment (relevant for dipole interactions). With full alignment, the optimization never converges because the alignment prevents any rotation. However, disabling alignment all-together causes images from a COS calculation to all have different orientations.

To remedy this, it was necessary to add a static variable to the `procrustes` function responsible for the alignment to allow for a partial alignment by mixing an identity matrix with the rotation matrix.

author: Marclie <mliebenthal@fsu.edu>
commit message:
When setting the `pal` flag and using the Dask scheduler, the calculations for each worker all set the same pal. This is an issue when running multiple concurrent calculations on the same machine and using `pal > 1`; depending on the number of dask workers and the `pal` value, the runtimes slowdown by over-subscribing the threads.

Instead, the `pal` flag now sets a maximum number of threads that is evenly distributed among the number of workers. This allows for single calculations to use all available threads and for batch calculations to evenly use the available threads.

unnecessary calculations, when accessing tangents, deciding upon a

underlying images were accessed in various methods, leading to
unexpected initiations of actual calculations, even in one optimization

commit message:
bugfix that lead to huge headaches and hours of wasted CI time ;)
setting coords3d after prim_internals led to a reset of the latter.
when prim_internals was accessed next time they were freshly calculated,
but the actual values of the dihedrals were lost. dihedrals are
periodic, so dihedral(-1.1pi) == dihedral(0.9pi). when the original
dihedral was -1.1pi, reset and the recalculated it would become 0.9pi,
which lead to huge (artificial) steps.

when coords3d is updated before prim_internals everything is fine. lol.

mod: refactor fit_rigid/procrustes calls out of Optimizer.optimize()

in preparation of calculating gradients/energies etc. outside of
Optimizer.optimize(), similar to how it is done in the IRC classes.

If align is set to True in COS optimizations, then the Optimizer base
class will call fit_rigid/_fit_rigid in the main optimization loop.
Child-classes can implement additional logic by implementing
Optimizer.fit_rigid(). If the method is not present, the optimizer will
fall back to self._fit_rigid(), that aligns coordinates, steps and
forces.

commit message:
mod: massive refactoring of COS classes

The previous design of various classes in pysisyphus.cos lead to
unnecessary calculations, when accessing tangents, deciding upon a
climbing image etc. The 'forces' and 'energy' attributes of the
underlying images were accessed in various methods, leading to
unexpected initiations of actual calculations, even in one optimization
cycle.

mod: Optimizer.geometry.prepare_opt_cycle is now called the call to
Optimizer.housekeeping() w/ the actual energies and gradients that are
valid for the current cycle. Previously,
Optimizer.geometry.prepare_opt_cycle() was only called w/ energies & its
derivatives from the previous cycle.

mod: Optimizer now passes energies of the current cycle to
Optimizer.geometry.reparametrize() calls. These energy values can be
used to determine climbing_image indices.
mod: Calculator.run() now keeps tracks of its numbers of invocation in
the dict self.Calculator.run_call_counts

commit message:
add: calculation of hindered rotor partition functions

using Gaussian Process Regression w/ sklearn and optuna for
hyperparameter optimization.
See "tests/test_hindered_rotor/test_gpr_torsion.py" for a simple
example.

The general idea is to calculate the torsional potential energy curve
on-the-fly at points, predicted by an acquisition function, based on a
Gaussian process regression.

When the potential energy curve is in place, nuclear wavefunctions and
associated eigenvalues are evaluated using a periodic 1d-Numerov
approach. The required mass is determined according to Pitzer/East/Radom
(see partfuncs.inertmom).

commit message:
add: calculation of hindered rotor partition functions

using Gaussian Process Regression w/ sklearn and optuna for
hyperparameter optimization.
See "tests/test_hindered_rotor/test_gpr_torsion.py" for a simple
example.

The general idea is to calculate the torsional potential energy curve
on-the-fly at points, predicted by an acquisition function, based on a
Gaussian process regression.

When the potential energy curve is in place, nuclear wavefunctions and
associated eigenvalues are evaluated using a periodic 1d-Numerov
approach. The required mass is determined according to Pitzer/East/Radom
(see partfuncs.inertmom).

commit message:
mod: massive refactoring of COS classes

The previous design of various classes in pysisyphus.cos lead to
unnecessary calculations, when accessing tangents, deciding upon a
climbing image etc. The 'forces' and 'energy' attributes of the
underlying images were accessed in various methods, leading to
unexpected initiations of actual calculations, even in one optimization
cycle.

mod: Optimizer.geometry.prepare_opt_cycle is now called the call to
Optimizer.housekeeping() w/ the actual energies and gradients that are
valid for the current cycle. Previously,
Optimizer.geometry.prepare_opt_cycle() was only called w/ energies & its
derivatives from the previous cycle.

mod: Optimizer now passes energies of the current cycle to
Optimizer.geometry.reparametrize() calls. These energy values can be
used to determine climbing_image indices.
mod: Calculator.run() now keeps tracks of its numbers of invocation in
the dict self.Calculator.run_call_counts

diabatization and quadrupole moment integrals are also used in
diabatization.

commit message:
mod: massive refactoring of COS classes

The previous design of various classes in pysisyphus.cos lead to
unnecessary calculations, when accessing tangents, deciding upon a
climbing image etc. The 'forces' and 'energy' attributes of the
underlying images were accessed in various methods, leading to
unexpected initiations of actual calculations, even in one optimization
cycle.

mod: Optimizer.geometry.prepare_opt_cycle is now called the call to
Optimizer.housekeeping() w/ the actual energies and gradients that are
valid for the current cycle. Previously,
Optimizer.geometry.prepare_opt_cycle() was only called w/ energies & its
derivatives from the previous cycle.

mod: Optimizer now passes energies of the current cycle to
Optimizer.geometry.reparametrize() calls. These energy values can be
used to determine climbing_image indices.
mod: Calculator.run() now keeps tracks of its numbers of invocation in
the dict self.Calculator.run_call_counts

with the previous root) can be propagated along the COS. Along with the

add: ChainOfStates.propagate() to propagate root info along COS

COS, and not for the remaining images. By calculuating ES overlaps along
the COS, information about the correct roots (with the highest overlap
with the previous root) can be propagated along the COS. Along with the
root info chkfiles are also propagated from image to image

author: Johannes Steinmetzer <johannes.steinmetzer@uni-jena.de>
commit message:
add: new coordinate systems: cartesian/mwcartesian

pysisyphus defaults to Cartesian coordinates (coord_type: cart).
Disregarding translation & rotation Cartesians are quite privileged in a
sense that QC codes usually require them to specify molecular
geometries. Similarily, derivatives of the energy like gradients and
Hessians are easily derived from the respective Cartesian quantities.

So it is a good idea to always keep a set of unmodified Cartesian
quantities (coordinates, gradients, ...) that are easily accessed as
properties of Geometry. Right now this is not the case. When atoms are
frozen via "freeze_atoms" Cartesian forces accessed via
Geometry.cart_forces will be zeroed for frozen atoms. Also the
coordinate/gradient/Hessian matrices will be unnecessarily big, as
frozen coordinates are not actually removed. Currently, the Hessian
isn't even modified at all.

Overall, these problems could be rectified by treating Cartesian
coordiantes similar to the way, internal coordinates are treated right
now: in a separate class that provides methods to transform
coordinates/forces etc. to the actual coordinates that are seen by
optimizers.

This commit provides a new CartesianCoords class that implement
Cartesians w/ support for freezing atoms and mass-weighing (coord_type:
cartesians/mwcartesians).

Fully switchting pysisyphus to utilize these new coord_types will
require quite some work & refactoring.

commit message:
mod: use numba multipole backend by default

currently, this only supports multipole integrals to arbitrary order,
but they are much faster than the python/numpy integrals and can be
evaluated in parallel. the ability to evaluate (overlap, dipole and
quadrupole) integrals will already bring us very far. Overlap integrals
are used for the Wavefunction sanity check, dipole integrals are used to
calculate (transition) dipole moments used in spectra plotting and
diabatization and quadrupole moment integrals are also used in
diabatization.

mod: updates to Jacobi-Sweep driver

also be passed to the driver. I couldn't really make the Jacobi-Sweeps
work for all different methods at the same time
(Foster-Boys/Edmiston-Ruedenberg/Pipek-Mezey) using the same gamma_func.

changes to some quantities.

loop. Previously it was only calculated after the first rotation, so the
initial value of the cost-function was never reported.

commit message:
add: ChainOfStates.propagate() to propagate root info along COS

Usually, a root of interest is only known for the first geometry of a
COS, and not for the remaining images. By calculuating ES overlaps along
the COS, information about the correct roots (with the highest overlap
with the previous root) can be propagated along the COS. Along with the
root info chkfiles are also propagated from image to image

direction and the other required arguments.

commit message:
Refactoring (#77)

- STAR & Hisat2 now use the annotation files for a splice-aware index

### Changed
- sizes removed from default config
- `genomepy FUNCTION --help` texts expanded
- all genomepy classes exported when imported into Python
- all providers now let you know when they are downloading assembly information.
- more descriptive feedback to installing & many errors

### Removed
- Old tests
- Removed outdated dependency `xmltodict`

### Fixed
- `genomepy config` options made more robust
- README.txt will no longer:
  - update 3x for each command
  - drop regex info
  - have duplicate lines

### Refactoring
- Genome class moved to `genome.py`
- Many functions moved to `utils.py`
- Many other functions made static methods of a class
- `Genome.track2fasta` and `Genome.get_random_sequence` optimized
- All Provider classes now store their genomes as a dict-in-dict, with the assembly name as key.
- Many Provider class functions now standardized. Many functions moved to from the daughter classes to the ProviderBase class.
- README.txt file generation and updating standardized
- Unit tests! all functions now have an individual test. Almost all test use functions already tested prior to them.
- Old tests incorporated in several extra tests (e01, e02, e03).
- Raise statements now use more fitting errors
- All instances of `os.remove` exchanged for `os.unlink`
- Almost all warnings fixed
- Extensive, COVID19-enabled, and somewhat pointless alphabetizing, optimizing and/or organizing changes to
    - imports everywhere
    - `.gitignore`
    - `.travis.yml`
    - `release_checklist.md`
    - `cli.py`
    - strings (many strings with .format() replaced with f-strings)

commit message:
Conditionally Cythonize the sources

This commit introduces an environment variable CYTHONIZE to control
whether to use Cython to generate the C code.

For example, the following will call Cython to generate the C code and
create source code tarball and wheel, useful for code release:

    CYTHONIZE=1 python setup.py sdist bdist_wheel

This command requires Cython (and other requirements) is available. When
Cython is not found, it warns the user to run:

    pip install -r requirements.txt

Alternatively, one can install cyvcf2 from the releases (``.tar.gz`` or
``.whl``),  this installation should not require Cython since the
generated C code has been included or compiled. For example,

    pip install dist/cyvcf2.tar.gz

This command now also correctly installs numpy, click, and other
dependencies.

author: Marcel Martin <marcel.martin@scilifelab.se>
commit message:
Install setup_requires dependencies with pip

The setup.py script needs to import Cython and numpy, but these are not
available when the setup.py script is run. The setuptools solution to this
is to add a setup_requires parameter to setup(). That has some problems
because it bypasses pip and installs dependencies with easy_install.
That does not know anything about wheels and is therefore a lot slower,
in particular when installing numpy.
<https://pip.pypa.io/en/latest/reference/pip_install/> has some warnings
about setup_requires.

The approach here is to spawn a 'pip install' process as part of
setup.py, as proposed by Daniel Holth in
<https://mail.python.org/pipermail/distutils-sig/2014-May/024391.html>.
The code is at <https://bitbucket.org/dholth/setup-requires/src>.
It is definitely a hack, but it seems to work well.

More discussions about setup_requires:
https://www.mail-archive.com/distutils-sig@python.org/msg25121.html
https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/1820

Closes #28.

example, `pip install cyvcf2` with either one of the dependencies
missing fails with an `ImportError`. The issue arises since setuptools
requires parsing `setup.py` once before any install occurs, in order to
detect the dependency structure.

This patch allows missing dependencies when parsing `setup.py`, and
separates a) installing missing dependencies and b) build extensions
which require these dependencies to be present.

commit message:
Conditionally Cythonize the sources (#143)

This commit introduces an environment variable CYTHONIZE to control
whether to use Cython to generate the C code.

For example, the following will call Cython to generate the C code and
create source code tarball and wheel, useful for code release:

    CYTHONIZE=1 python setup.py sdist bdist_wheel

This command requires Cython (and other requirements) is available. When
Cython is not found, it warns the user to run:

    pip install -r requirements.txt

Alternatively, one can install cyvcf2 from the releases (``.tar.gz`` or
``.whl``),  this installation should not require Cython since the
generated C code has been included or compiled. For example,

    pip install dist/cyvcf2.tar.gz

This command now also correctly installs numpy, click, and other
dependencies.

commit message:
release gil:

this and the previous changes release the gil around critical sections of iteration
over a VCF. Those are intializing an iterator and parsing the bcf_record, either
from a tabixy query or just straight iteration.

In my test, I can create a threadpool, each with it's own vcf object, do region queries
in parallel and get near perfect parallelism with 16 threads.

Because cyvcf2 objects are not serializable, python threads are the only way to parallelize
operations of a VCF.

commit message:
Two new implementations of the measure_cphase method in multi_qubit_module.py:

measure_cphase_new: Implements a 2D sweep with phases in the first and [flux length,flux amplitude] in the second dimension.
In order to get this working, the axis argument of np.repeat in  MC.tile_sweep_points_for_2D() has been added and set to 0. This enables correct repetition of a multi parameter array and should not affect the single parameter case.

new hard sweep: Flux_pulse_CPhase_hard_swf_new
new pulse sequence: flux_pulse_CPhase_seq_new in fluxing_sequences.py

Alternative measurement function:

measure_cphase_new2: Performing a loop over X90 phases on target qubit.
Withing the loop, the [flux_length,flux_amp] values are swept in a regular 2 parameter 1D sweep.
This is most likely faster.

additional hard sweep function: Flux_pulse_Cphase_hard_swf_new2
additional pulse sequence: flux_pulse_CPhase_seq_new2

In: multi_qubit_module.py: cphase_gate_tuneup_predictive: New optimization method to tuneup cphase gates using a pool of predictive algorithms.

author: lciorciaro <casyi@me.com>
commit message:
fix ordering of channels in UHFQC detector function (#355)

the channels where put in an array by looping over dict.keys(), which was not guaranteed to preserve ordering.

It should work. The ordering is determined in a bit of a round-about way, and could and should probably be arranged a bit clearer. This PR is just a minimum-number-of-lines hotfix of the problem.

Here is how it goes:
UHFQC.acquisition_initialize sets UHFQC.acquisition_paths (strings) according to a list of channels given to it (which are integers), (preserving the order).

acquisition_poll returns a dictionary; the keys of that dictionary are integers, but they are not channels, but indices into acquisition_paths (and thus channels, which has the same order). Looping over these keys as sorted when interpreting the data in the detector thus arranges the returned data in the same order in which channels are passed to acquisition_initialize.

commit message:
Cleanup and refactorings as per @AdriaanRol review for pull request.

- Inherit from SCPI, like the AWG driver.
- Added parameter docstrings and extended module documentation.
- Where applicable added units.
- Removed parameters from the driver that have no prio yet.
- Removed commands for temperature setpoints (of the heating PID controllers)
  because we probably don't want to allow for changing those.
- No validators for getters. (why are there validators on the driver side at all?)
- Removed `__main__` block from module.
- Calibration commands for each qubit separately, to keep things simple. This
  can be extended later when requested.
- During development, internal VSM logs can be viewed by pointing a
  webbrowser to port 5000 of the VSM, example: http://192.168.0.10:5000/
  For normal use, this will probably be restricted/disabled.
- Some code-yoga to adhere to PEP8 :)

author: Jeroen Bergmans <bergmansj@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Feature/qutech vsm driver (#396)

* Start feature branch adding the VSM driver to PycQED

* Rename module to conform to the other modules.

* Leave out silly custom validator

* Ignore PyCharm crud.

* Cleanup and refactorings as per @AdriaanRol review for pull request.

- Inherit from SCPI, like the AWG driver.
- Added parameter docstrings and extended module documentation.
- Where applicable added units.
- Removed parameters from the driver that have no prio yet.
- Removed commands for temperature setpoints (of the heating PID controllers)
  because we probably don't want to allow for changing those.
- No validators for getters. (why are there validators on the driver side at all?)
- Removed `__main__` block from module.
- Calibration commands for each qubit separately, to keep things simple. This
  can be extended later when requested.
- During development, internal VSM logs can be viewed by pointing a
  webbrowser to port 5000 of the VSM, example: http://192.168.0.10:5000/
  For normal use, this will probably be restricted/disabled.
- Some code-yoga to adhere to PEP8 :)

* Removed per channel marker source

* Added get_parsers

* typo

* Frequencies are float, not int.

New way of handling hyperparameters in the predictive methods.

Hyperparameters are now input as dictionaries containing the required paramters of the corresponding estimator class.
This avoids having to deal with many keyword arguments and cleans up the code.

Additionally: The GRNN_neupy estimator handles now multiple target parameters. This is achieved by training new instance of GRNN for each target parameter on the complete training data.

These changes are committed here as they serve the new CPhase tuneup functionality developed on this branch.

commit message:
The type system now stores enough type information to check for intersections (useful for upcoming scope analysis).

Also fixed the following bugs:

1. Non-boolean constraints now fail.

  eg.
  [1 - 3]

2. "this" is now handled correctly.

  eg.
  A
    B ?
      C
    [A.B.this.C]

  will now fail.

3. Multiple (implicit) refs are now handled correctly.

  eg.
  A -> B
  B -> C
  C -> int

  [A = B]

  now produces the correct/runnable output.

4. Correctly handles unions of different types.

  eg.
  A
  C -> int

  [(A++C) = 1]

  will now pass type checking (it would fail before) and produce the correct output.

5. If/then/else now correctly handles nonboolean consequents and alternatives.

  eg.
  C -> int
  [(if (C=5) then 3 else 4) = 3]

6. Correctly handles explicit refs

  eg.
  A -> B
  B -> int

  [A.ref.ref = B.ref]

  will produce the correct output

should be. The exception error in getPropAtom is modifying to be
